title: Design System: Budget Tracker
note: This sidecar normally lives at .impeccable/design.json. That directory is root-owned and unwritable in this repo, so it is written beside DESIGN.md at the project root.

paper.purpose: The page ground. Never a component fill.

sheet.purpose: The surface laid on the stock: every sheet, control, menu, dialog and toast.

sheet-alt.purpose: Column-head rows, row hover, ghost-button hover, pace-bar trough.

rule.purpose: The default 1px rule; set as the global border-color so a bare border is always correct.

rule-strong.purpose: Register head, first entry of a new day, secondary-button outline, control hover, chart axis, scrollbar thumb.

perforation.purpose: The stub-edge perforation gradient. Currently declared but not deployed by any component.

ink.purpose: Body text, figures, paid-out bars, the elapsed rule's fill, total borders, and the heaviest frame.

ink-3.purpose: Column heads, the Courier stamp layer, notes, placeholders, blank-cell dashes.

carbon.purpose: The committed ink: primary buttons, active nav, focus ring, caret, selected segment, paid-in bars, in-sheet links.

carbon-2.purpose: Primary hover, and a budget bar running ahead of pace.

carbon-tint.purpose: The only interactive fill in the system: active nav row, drag drop-target, the opening frame of entry-strike.

red.purpose: Trouble only: a negative figure, an over-limit bar, a field in error, delete, the irreversible block.

red-tint.purpose: Ground of an invalid field and resting fill of the danger button.

display.purpose: The one money figure a page exists to report. 30px, 38px from sm. One per page, never two.

headline.purpose: The statement head's title. One per page.

title.purpose: The printed head of a sheet or dialog; also the shape of buttons and nav items.

body.purpose: Register lines, field values, descriptions. 13px Archivo.

note.purpose: Hints, verdict lines, honesty footnotes. 11px, usually ink-3.

label.purpose: The .col-head class: a printed head above a table column or above a figure.

stamp.purpose: The .stamp class — Courier Prime reference layer: dates, period status, section numerals, TFR/IN tags. Used only at 9–11px.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system has zero shadows in any component or state. Depth is rule weight and stock tone.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: The modal backdrop — the single non-flat surface treatment in the build. Fades in over 160ms.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The easing for both entrances: sheet-in and entry-strike.

motion.name: sheet-in
motion.purpose: Utility entrance (.animate-in): 6px rise and fade for page content, dialogs, menus, toasts.

motion.name: entry-strike
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: a new entry struck onto the sheet from the left, opening on a carbon-tint ground that clears as it settles.

motion.name: bar-width
motion.purpose: The elapsed rule and the pace bar filling.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation and transition collapses globally.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: The workhorse. The register's single Amount column splits into Paid out / Paid in / Transfer / Balance; padding steps up; dialogs centre.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Navigation moves from the foot (tab bar) to the left edge (sidebar); two-up sheet grids appear.

narrative.overview:
This is an account book, not a dashboard. The governing fiction is a bank passbook printed on cheque safety-tint stock: pale green paper, a whiter sheet laid on it, hairline rules dividing columns, and two inks doing all the work — the ledger's black and the carbon-copy blue of a committed entry. Every figure is money in a column, so no figure may ever shift; every entry carries the balance it left behind, so "how am I doing" is answered by the register's own construction rather than by a row of stat cards.

The system's discipline is subtractive. It refuses the KPI-card row, the donut, the tinted status pill, and the coloured category chip — not as taste, but because each of them spends colour on identity, and in this world colour is reserved for one meaning: trouble. Income and expense are separated by column position, the way a real register separates them; that frees red to mean exactly one thing everywhere it appears. The rest of the interface is structure: ruled rows, printed column heads, stamped reference codes. Density is high and deliberate, because a book of accounts is meant to be read down, not scanned across.

Dark mode is not an inversion. It is the carbon copy underneath the top sheet: the same document, printed through, warmer greys and a lighter blue ink. The two themes are two sides of one artefact, and the theme control names them that way ("Sheet", "Carbon").
keyCharacteristics: Cheque safety-tint stock with a whiter sheet laid on it; no gradients, no glass, no tint fills except the two semantic tints.
Two inks: ledger black for structure and figures, carbon blue for the committed and the interactive.
Ledger red spent on one meaning only — money you do not have, or a limit you have passed.
Hairline rules and ruled columns instead of cards; square corners everywhere; zero shadows.
Archivo for reading, Archivo Narrow stamped in uppercase for heads and controls, Courier Prime for the machine-stamped reference layer.
Tabular lining figures in every table, right-aligned on a shared decimal.
One display step, one authored motion moment, one global instrument (the elapsed rule).

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Colour carries exactly one meaning in this app: trouble. Direction of money is read from column position, never from green-versus-red. If a new surface needs to distinguish income from expense, it gets another column or a ruled tag — not a hue.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Every mark is ledger black or carbon blue. Ink is structure, figures and the printed page; carbon is what the user has committed to or is standing on. A third accent has no role to fill and must not be introduced.

rules.name: The Colour-As-Subject Rule
rules.body: Category colour appears in exactly two places: the categories index, where the colour is the thing being edited, and a chart where colour is the only encoding available. It is deliberately absent from the register, the analysis table and the budget bars.

rules.name: The Carbon Copy Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is the same document printed through, not an inversion. Dark tokens keep the light theme's roles intact — stock stays below sheet, rule stays below rule-strong, carbon stays the committed ink.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums applies to every table and every .figure at the base layer. A figure that shifts as it updates has broken the column, and the column is the whole argument of this design.

rules.name: The One Display Step Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one display size and exactly one display figure per page. If a second figure wants to be big, the page has two subjects and one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Stamped Head Rule
rules.body: Headings, buttons, nav and column heads are always Archivo Narrow, uppercase, letterspaced. Sentence-case headings and body-weight buttons do not exist in this world.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No kicker or eyebrow above a heading, on any navigation surface. A .col-head above a figure is native to the world and correct — a decorative label above a heading is not the same device and is not permitted.

rules.name: The Ruled Row Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from hairlines between rows, not from gaps between boxes. A list is a sequence of bordered rows inside one sheet; it is never a stack of separated tiles.

rules.name: The Column-Position Rule
rules.body: In any table of money, direction is encoded by which column the figure lands in. Below sm, where the columns collapse into one, direction moves onto a ruled stamp tag (TFR, IN) — a small printed object on the sheet, never a colour and never a whisper.

rules.name: The One Navigation Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one navigation at every width: sidebar at lg and above, tab bar below it. No band where the app has two, none where it has none.

rules.name: The Flat Book Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, ever, in any state. Something that needs to read as "on top" gets border-ink; something that needs to read as "different ground" gets sheet-alt.

rules.name: The Total Rule
rules.body: A figure that closes an arithmetic is separated by a 2px ink top border. That heavier rule is reserved for totals (and, in red, for the irreversible block); it must not be used for ordinary emphasis.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius 0 on everything. If a component needs to look softer, it is the wrong component for this world.

rules.name: The Hatch Rule
rules.body: 45° hatching means "incomplete or past the boundary" and nothing else. A partial period is hatched rather than drawn solid, because a partial bar flush beside complete ones is the most misleading mark this app could print.

rules.name: The One Authored Moment Rule
rules.body: entry-strike is the system's only expressive animation, and it belongs to recording an entry — the product's hot path. Everything else either fades in or does not move. A second authored moment would make the first one ordinary.

dos: Do put every money figure through Amount, and every table under tabular-nums lining-nums. Right-align on a shared decimal.
Do encode direction with column position, and give a collapsed mobile column a ruled .stamp tag (TFR, IN) instead of a colour.
Do build new surfaces from Sheet + ruled rows: one hairline between rows, edge-to-edge, the sheet supplying horizontal padding.
Do reserve --red for money you do not have or a limit already passed, and pair it with a written word or the DR marker so meaning never rests on hue.
Do write the verdict out in words next to any bar or gauge ("£40 within pace"), so the reader never has to compute a judgement from a colour.
Do hatch anything that is incomplete or past its boundary, at 45°.
Do keep one display figure per page, and let the elapsed rule in the statement head be the only global instrument.
Do state the period's honesty in plain 11px prose under a summary when a comparison has been cut to a like-for-like day range.
Do frame anything laid over the book with border-ink, and let hover change ground (sheet-alt) or border weight.
donts: Don't add a shadow, a radius, or a gradient. Not on hover, not on a dialog, not "just a subtle one".
Don't nest a Sheet inside a Sheet, or reintroduce the card — a row of stat tiles is the specific thing the summary block exists to replace.
Don't use green-for-income / red-for-expense, or any second accent colour. Colour means trouble; that is its whole job.
Don't print category colour in the register, the analysis table, or a budget bar. Its only homes are the categories index and a chart where colour is the sole encoding.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading in a navigation surface. (A .col-head above a figure is a column head, and is correct.)
Don't set a heading, button or nav label in body case or body weight — those are always Archivo Narrow, uppercase, letterspaced.
Don't introduce a second display size, or a second big figure on a page.
Don't author a second signature animation; extend entry-strike's meaning instead, or use animate-in.
Don't draw a partial period flush beside complete ones, or clamp an overspent bar at 100%. Both flatter the user with an artefact of timing.
Don't reveal controls only on hover — a touch device has no hover to reveal them with.
